lawyer:
MA Quddus Sheikh ----- For the Petitioner 
Sukumar Biswas. AAG ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Younus Mia (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Chairman, 1st Court of Settlement and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh this Rule Nisi was issued at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned judgment dated 10-9-2001 (Annexure- "C" to the petition) should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the case house No. 25/19, Block -D, Mohammadpur, Dhaka should not be released from the 'Kha" list of abandoned buildings published on 23-9-86 and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this rule is, in abridge, is that, the Government of the then East Pakistan allotted the house in question and leased out the property in favour of one Abdul Wahid, son of late Yasin for a period of 99 years and accordingly a lease deed was executed and registered on 11-5-1961 being deed No. 2567. After leasing out of the property in favour of said Abdul Wahid he got delivery of possession and got his name mutated in the relevant khatian and paid rents to the Government and other utility bills to different authorities. Said Abdul Wahid while in possession and enjoyment of the property died on 15-10-1967 leaving his only heir wife Jamila Khatun to inherit him. After the death of Abdul Wahid his wife Jamila Khatun obtained succession certificate from the 3rd Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka in Succession Certificate Case No.991 of 1984. While Jamila Khatun was in possession and enjoyment of the property she transferred the same for a valuable consideration to the petitioner on 19-11-1985 by a registered deed No. 3489 and delivered possession to the petitioner. After purchase the petitioner got his name mutated in the khatian and paid all taxes and utility bills to the Government and other statutory authorities.

3. While the petitioner has been enjoying and possessing the property all on a sudden he came to know that the property has been includedin the "Kha" list of the abandoned property published on 23-5-1985 without service of any notice upon the petitioner as required by law. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application before the Court of settlement challenging inclusion of the property in question in the "Kha" list of the abandoned properties which was registered as settlement Case No. 493 of 1988. The case was fixed for hearing on 23-11-1993 amongst other dates and on the date fixed none appeared before the Court of settlement. Consequently the case was dismissed for default. Thereafter, the petitioner being aggrieved with the order of dismissal filed Writ Petition No. 1057 of 1994 before this Court against the order of dismissal. The said petition was heard by this Court and after contested hearing, rule was made absolute and the case was sent back on remand to the Court of settlement for rehearing. Upon receipt of the judgment of this Court, the Court of settlement fixed the case for hearing on 10-9-2001. On the date fixed the conducting lawyer for the petitioner due to his personal difficulties filed an application before the Court of settlement, seeking adjournment through his junior friend Advocate Mr Mahbub Ali Said Advocate Mr Mahbub Ali due to his urgent need left the Court requesting one Mr Nazrul Islam Chowdhury to move the application but unfortunately he did not move the application. Consequently the case was dismissed on merit. The petitioner further stated that he has no negligence and laches on his part and has no knowledge about the date of hearing of the case. Had it been known to him he would have appeared and moved the petition and in that event the case would not have been dismissed. It is also stated that the order of dismissal has caused a serious injustice to the petitioner and at this stage being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 10-9- 2001 the petitioner moved before this Court with this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule and order of status quo. During pendency of the Rule petitioner Md Younus Mia died and his heirs have been substituted as petitioners vide order dated 26-2-2009.

4. Respondent No.2 Government contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia that original owner who got allotment of the house left the country before war of independence and the property has been declared abandoned under PO 16 of 1972 and listed in the "Kha" list published on 23-9-1968 under the provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance 54 of 1985. The petitioners filed the instant writ petition only to grab the Government property. The claimant petitioner Md Younus Mia hopelessly failed to prove his case by adducing any evidence before the Court of settlement and also failed to pursue the case diligently and for his laches the case was dismissed on merit considering the evidences on record. As such the Rule is liable to be discharged.

5. Mr MA Quddus Sheikh, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the claimant petitioner late Md Younus Mia has had no laches or negligence on his part on the date fixed when the case was taken up for hearing by the Court of settlement and explained the situation why the application for adjournment of hearing was not moved when the case was called for hearing. He next submits that the impugned judgment passed by the Court of settlement dismissing the case is palpably illegal though the judgment has been designed as passed on merit but in fact it does not contain any decision regarding the issue whether the property in question was legally included in the list of the abandoned property. He further submits that sub-section 5 of section 10 of Ordinance No.54 of 1985 provides that the Court of settlement ought to have given a decision on merit in the case irrespective of non- appearance ofthe parties but in the instant case no such decision has been given by the Court of settlement as per provision of law and as such the impugned judgment is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In support of his submission he referred the decisions in Bangladesh vs Md Hafizur Rahman reported in 53 DLR (AD) 99, Chand Mia vs Chairman, The Court of Settlement reported in 45 DLR 304 and Bangladesh vs Shamsul Hoque reported in 56 DLR (AD) 101.

6. On the other hand, Mr Sukumar Biswas, the learned Assistant-Attorney-General appearing for the State opposing the Rule submits that since the petitioner Md Younus Mia was found absent when the case was called on for hearing, the Court of settlement had no other alternative but to dismiss the case. He further submits that the Court of settlement dismissed the case considering past and present conduct of the petitioner and discussed merit of the case and, as such, the Court of settlement committed no illegality in passing the judgment and order in question.

7. Learned Assistant Attorney-General further submits that in a proceeding under section 7, the entire onus is on the person claiming any right or interest in a building included in the list to show that the building is not an abandoned property and has not vested in the Government under PO 16 of 1972 or that his right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of that Order. He further asserts that the very fact of inclusion of a building in the list of abandoned property is in itself proof that the property is an abandoned property and the Government has nothing to prove or deny and consequentially it is for the aggrieved person to establish his claim by whatever evidence he chooses to produce. It is argued that the denial of a fair trial will only arise if an opportunity is not afforded to the person allowing him to produce his evidence 054r any evidence sought to be adduced by him is unreasonably refused or he is not given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. He further submits that the Court of settlement in its impugned judgment clearly observed that the petitioner is a habitual defaulter and he utterly failed to pursue the case and to produce evidences both oral and documentary and, as such, the Court of settlement rightly dismissed the case of the petitioner and there was no illegality. In support of his submission he referred the cases of Bangladesh vs Ms Laila Ahmed vs The Court of Settlement reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71, Government of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil reported in 48 DLR (AD) 10 and Secretary, Ministry of Works vs Rowshan Ara Begum reported in 57 DLR (AD) 167.

8. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the application, impugned judgment and order and other annexure appended to the petition.

9. Sub-section-5 of section-10 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 speaks as to how a Court of settlement shall determine and decide a case filed by a person before it. To appreciate the provision, sub-section-5 of section 10 is quoted below:-

"A Court of settlement shall, after such enquiry as it may deem necessary and after giving opportunity to the parties concerned of being heard and also adducing evidence , both oral and documentary, if any, make such decision on the prayer of the application as it deems fit".

10. According to the provision as quoted above the Ordinance gives power of investigation and provides a provision for giving a reasonable opportunity to the party not only of being heard but also to give an opportunity to adduce evidence both oral and documentary. In the instant case we are to see whether the reasonable opportunities were given to the parties to prove their case. In this case finality has been given to a decision of the Court of settlement which is binding on the parties. In such scheme of the Ordinance one can legitimately make a grievance that an opportunity of fair trial must be given while disposing the case.

11. From perusal of the judgment it appears that there is nothing on record particularly from the judgment of Court of settlement that there was any hearing conducted in the matter and that any opportunity was provided to the parties to place the case or adducing the evidences. The judgment of the Court of settlement only speaks about the conduct of the petitioner which encouraged the Court to dismiss the case. The Court of settlement in disposing a case before it in the absence of any party ought to have given decision on merit holding that the property was rightly included in the list of the abandoned property but in the present case we find no such decision regarding the issue whether the said property was legally included in the list or not although it appears that even from the plain reading of the sub-section 5 of section 10 of the Ordinance, 1985, the Court of settlement ought to have given such decision. Under the said provision of law the Court of settlement is not empowered to dismiss the case pending before it without giving any decision on merit. From perusal of the impugned judgment we do not find that anything in rebuttal was adduced by the Government challenging the contents of the petition. We do not find anything in the judgment itself from where a conclusion can be drawn that the Court of settlement independently decided the question of abandoned character of the property other than commenting on the conduct of the petitioner. In the circumstance we have no hesitation in holding that sub-section 5 of section .10 of the Ordinance has been totally ignored in deciding the case.

12. The Court of settlement has full legal authority to determine the question regarding the abandoned character of the building affecting the rights of the parties. The Ordinance imposes a duty on it to act judicially and the Court of settlement acted in violation of the principles of natural justice and norms of fair trial and failed to act in accordance with the jurisdiction vested in it by law. The law requires that a decision shall have to be given on the issue and having not been given in the instant case the impugned judgment and order passed by the Court of settlement must be held to be without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and consequently the case must be sent back to the Court of settlement for trial.

13. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

14. It is declared that the impugned judgment and order dated 10-9-2001 (Annexure-"C" to the petition) passed by the respondent No.1, in Settlement Case No. 493 of 1988 has been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The Court of settlement is directed to try the case and give a decision in accordance with law as indicated above giving reasonable opportunity to the parties concerned of being heard and adducing evidences both oral and documentary.

15. Before parting of it should be observed that the very conduct of the claimant petitioner now deceased Md Younus Mia as observed by the Court of settlement in its judgment and order, is really undesirable and the present petitioners are hereby directed to take proper steps to get the case heard and disposed of on the date of hearing fixed by the Court of settlement and in the event of failure of the petitioner to appear before the Court and produce evidence after being afforded opportunity to do so, the Court of settlement will be at liberty to dispose of the case on merit giving decisions as per provision of law.

16. The Order of status quo passed at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby recalled and stand vacated.

Communicate a copy of this judgment with LCR to the Court concerned immediately.

End.
